title: tune-nccl-async-collectives-and-kernel-scheduling-for-tensor-parallel-overlap
author: Diego Ramirez
description:
Motivation: Tensor-parallel multi-GPU inference suffers from suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and GPU kernel execution for several common model shapes. This PR tunes asynchronous NCCL usage, stream prioritization, and kernel scheduling heuristics to improve compute/communication overlap and reduce tail latency in 8/16-GPU TP setups.

What changed (high level): Updated NCCL manager to use dedicated async streams for long-running collectives with tuned priorities; introduced a cooperative kernel scheduling hint path that defers low-priority host-to-device work to avoid kernel sync stalls; reworked the stream synchronization points to minimize unnecessary cudaEvent waits; added a new lightweight runtime policy that chooses between eager and deferred collective execution based on sequence-length histogram and KV-cache hit patterns.

Why this approach: Previous conservative synchronization favored correctness but serialized communication and compute in several hot paths. By making collectives asynchronous on a dedicated stream and selecting when to rely on implicit stream ordering vs explicit events, we can keep compute kernels busy while NCCL progress occurs, yielding better utilization without sacrificing correctness. The policy uses telemetry already present in the runtime (seqlen distributions and cache hit ratios) to avoid regressions on short-sequence workloads.

Benchmark summary: Microbenchmarks on internal perf harness (gpt-like 20B, seq=1024, batch=1 effective tokens) on an 8x A100 node: throughput +9.7% p50 tokens/sec, tail (p99) latency -14.3%. Larger-scale 16-GPU TP runs show similar improvements (throughput +7-10%, p99 -10%). Short-sequence workloads (seq <= 128) are unchanged (within 1-2%) because the new policy keeps existing eager path. Memory and correctness: KV-cache behavior unchanged; no extra GPU memory observed in steady state.

Testing & validation: Unit tests for NCCL manager behavior and stream ordering added; CI GPU smoke tests run in the perf-canary lane. End-to-end perf harness tests included in benchlab matrix. Verified deterministic outputs against main for sampled prompts.

Risks & mitigations: Asynchronous collectives introduce more complex ordering assumptions. To mitigate we added conservative fallbacks: explicit event synchronization on a per-model-config basis (configurable via runtime flag redwood.runtime.nccl.async_override=false), and a telemetry alert that triggers canary rollback if per-route fidelity regressions are detected.

Related: ENG-4872 (tensor-parallel scheduling), ENG-4920 (nccl perf), PRs: pr-36845, pr-34021 for prior tuning iterations.
